subject: SecureForge evidence exchange + connector scope
messages:
From: Lakshmi Rao <lakshmi@secureforge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + evidence exchange for SecureForge onboarding

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking the call last week. SecureForge is excited about a potential partner connector that would automate pen-test and compliance artifact delivery into Redwood's evidence pipeline. Attached is a short SOW and an overview of how we currently package evidence for customers.

Quick highlights:
- We deliver redacted forensic artifacts, signed test reports, and artifact manifests (JSON)
- We can push to customer S3 buckets, or provide pre-signed URLs for pull-based retrieval
- Typical retention request from customers is 90 days, with optional longer-term escrow for archival requests

Would love to set a technical sync to scope the connector and confirm what metadata fields Redwood needs for mapping to SOC2/HIPAA evidence types.

Attachment: SecureForge-Intro-SOW.pdf (application/pdf)

Lakshmi Rao
Head of Alliances | SecureForge
lakshmi@secureforge.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + evidence exchange for SecureForge onboarding

Lakshmi — thanks for the SOW and summary. I looped in Kim and Marcus from our Assurance & Partner Integrations teams. A couple of clarifying items before we put engineers on a call:

1) Evidence transport: our preferred flow is a push model into a customer-owned S3 prefix with object tags for artifact_type, test_date, and sha256. We also support a partner API pull (pre-signed URLs) if push is not possible.
2) Metadata mapping: we need a mapping doc that lists the artifact_type values you publish. Typical Redwood fields: evidence_type, control_id, report_version, redaction_level.
3) KMS/keys: for private deployments we require customer-managed KMS; for hosted customers we can accept partner-signed artifacts but must surface who had key access.
4) Retention & TTL: please confirm whether SecureForge can honor per-customer TTL headers and an audit log of retrievals.

Can you share a sample artifact manifest (JSON) and a sample S3 key naming convention? If you can drop that into the Drive link below we'll take a look and propose a connector scope and pilot cadence.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSecureForgeOnboard
Attachment: redwood-evidence-requirements-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Next steps I propose:
- SecureForge shares schema + sample artifacts (we can review asynchronously)
- Technical sync (30-45m) next week with eng + assurance (Kim/Marcus)
- Pilot: one customer, 2-week run to validate mapping, retention, and access logs

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Vanessa / team — attaching the schema and an example manifest. A few notes inline: 

- We can publish artifacts to a customer S3 bucket under key: secureforge/<customer_id>/<scan_date>/<artifact_type>/<filename>. We include an accompanying manifest.json with per-file metadata and sha256.
- We support the following artifact_type values: penetration_report, vuln_scan_csv, exploit_proof, signed_manifest. We can add control_id tags if you provide your mapping table.
- TTL: we can set x-amz-restore/expiration metadata per object and emit a delivery_event (webhook) when the object is written.
- For hosted customers we propose signing manifests with a SecureForge key and publishing a signature file for Redwood to verify.

Attachment: secureforge-evidence-schema.json (application/json)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSecureForgeOnboard

Happy to do the tech sync Tuesday/Wednesday next week (we are PST-based). Proposed attendees from our side: Lakshmi (Alliances), Priyanka (Engineering), and Raj (Security).

—Partnerships Team
SecureForge

FYI — forwarding SecureForge's schema and our proposed connector approach. Quick asks for the Assurance and Integrations teams before we confirm the pilot customer: 

- Kim: can you confirm the minimum metadata mapping we need to treat an object as SOC2 evidence? Specifically which artifact_type -> control_id mappings are required.
- Marcus: engineering: estimate for a lightweight connector prototype (S3 manifest polling + object tagging ingestion). Ballpark sprint estimate?
- Karthik: procurement/legal: SecureForge's SOW references 30-day SLA for evidence handoff and a clause about retention escrow; any redlines we should flag early?

Proposed pilot acceptance criteria (draft):
- Successful ingestion of signed_manifest.json and mapping to evidence_type in Redwood
- Audit log entries for every retrieval and a proof-of-write event
- Retention honored per customer TTL (default 90 days)

If this is green I will schedule the tech sync for Tue 21 Sep 2027, 10am PT.

Vanessa — quick confirmation after scanning the schema:

- Metadata: we need at minimum evidence_type, control_id, report_date, origin_system, and signature_verified boolean. SecureForge's manifest covers most of this; we'll provide a short mapping table to return to them.
- Retention: 90 days TTL as a baseline is fine for a pilot. For customers needing longer we will route to escrow (legal + procurement approval required).
- Security: for hosted customers we accept signature verification; for Private deployments the SOW should require partner to publish to customer-managed S3 or use mutual TLS for the API.

Procurement note (Karthik): SecureForge's SOW mentions a 30-day SLA for initial delivery — that is operational and OK. The escrow/retention language needs to be tightened: add explicit deletion certification and audit window (we recommend 7-day deletion proof window). Also request DocuSign counter-sign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/placeholder-secureforge-sow

I recommend pilot scope: 1 customer, 3 artifact classes (penetration_report, signed_manifest, exploit_proof), TTL 90 days, signed manifests, and read-only retrieval logs retained for 180 days in our audit store. If accepted, Integrations (Marcus) can estimate a focused 2-sprint prototype.

Kim
Kimberly Park
